title: KAMI: Communication-Avoiding General Matrix Multiplication within a Single GPU
problem: Large-scale GEMM near peak GPU performance, but substantial optimization opportunities remain in small and batched GEMM operations.
motivation: Communication-avoiding techniques can improve small/batched GEMM through better memory hierarchy utilization within GPU.
method: KAMI reduces data movement during matrix multiplication on GPUs using three communication-avoiding approaches (1D, 2D, and 3D thread block configurations). For each approach, it stores intermediate results in different memory levels—thread registers (ultra-fast, one per core) and shared memory (fast, shared across a block)—and uses specialized tensor cores (hardware built into GPUs for fast matrix math). The framework also supports sparse variants called SpMM and SpGEMM for matrices with many zeros.
key_novelty: KAMI is the first to analyze communication-avoiding matrix multiplication at the GPU clock cycle level (counting individual GPU processing steps), providing a unified framework for dense, sparse, batched, and low-rank matrices.
contributions: Communication-avoiding GEMM algorithms (1D, 2D, 3D variants) for single GPU
Clock cycle-level performance analysis for GPUs
Support across NVIDIA, AMD, Intel GPUs

metrics.performance: significant improvement over cuBLAS, CUTLASS, MAGMA
